name: Reader output review
purpose: Grade what Lysilogy shows on the Abstract and Overview views for one paper, against the paper itself and the papers around it. Grade each component on its own before forming an overall view. Not produced is a real outcome: mark it and grade what that means for the reader.

anchors.0: Absent, wrong, or generic enough to fit an unrelated paper.
anchors.1: Some relevant content, but mostly labels, restatement, or confident claims with nothing behind them.
anchors.2: Specific to this paper and broadly useful, with important gaps or errors a careful reader would notice.
anchors.3: Strong: accurate, specific, and useful to a smart outsider; minor lapses only.
anchors.4: Exceptional: precise and economical; you would not rewrite it.

components.label: Abstract
components.question: Is the text shown as the authors' abstract exactly the authors' abstract?
components.guidance: Compare with the PDF's first page, or with the oracle abstract when the manifest names one. Whitespace, hyphenation at line ends and ligatures do not count as errors; dropped or added sentences do.

dimensions.label: Exactly the abstract
dimensions.question: All of the authors' abstract and nothing else?

dimensions.label: What went wrong
dimensions.question: The main failure, when it is not exact.

options.label: Extra text: keywords, affiliations, introduction, footnotes
Wrong block: not the abstract at all
Garbled: order, encoding or column interleaving
Missing: no abstract although the paper has one

components.label: Thesis line
components.question: Does the one-line thesis state what this paper contributes, in words a smart outsider understands?

dimensions.label: Faithful and specific
dimensions.question: Accurate to the paper and impossible to paste onto a different one?

anchors.0: Wrong, or a generic topic label.
anchors.2: Right topic and roughly right claim, but vague or overstated.
anchors.4: States the actual contribution and its scope in one sentence.

components.label: Why it matters
components.question: After reading the context on the first view, do you know why this paper matters: what came before, what it changed, and what to read alongside it?
components.guidance: This is the highest-value component. Judge it against the neighbours listed in the manifest and your own knowledge. A single false claim about the field is a hard reject, however good the rest is.

hard_reject.label: Contains a false claim
hard_reject.question: Is any consequential statement about the paper's history, reception, priority or influence false?

dimensions.label: Accuracy
dimensions.question: Is what it says about the field before and after the paper true?

anchors.1: Gets the outline of the history wrong in a way that would mislead.
anchors.2: True in outline, with a wrong date, attribution or emphasis.
anchors.4: Everything checks out, including who did what and when.

dimensions.label: Orientation
dimensions.question: Could you now explain to a colleague why this paper is worth reading and what it changed, in terms that fit only this paper?

anchors.0: Generic enough to paste onto another paper in the field ('an influential paper that sparked much follow-up work'), or a restatement of the abstract.
anchors.2: Names the right debate or predecessor but not what this paper did to it; useful but padded.
anchors.4: Names the specific prior belief, method or result this paper displaced or extended, and what the field did next; nearly every sentence adds something the abstract does not.

dimensions.label: Read-alongside papers
dimensions.question: Are the suggested surrounding papers the right ones, each with a true one-line reason?

anchors.0: None given, invented papers, or the wrong ones.
anchors.2: Real and relevant, but missing the obvious predecessor, successor or critique.
anchors.4: The papers you would hand a newcomer, each with an accurate reason.

dimensions.label: Honest about the unknown
dimensions.question: Are the background and citation-graph labels right, and does it admit what it does not know about the paper's reception instead of asserting influence?

components.label: Outline
components.question: Does the outline list the paper's sections as printed, with the right levels and pages?
components.guidance: Count against the printed headings in the PDF. Front matter, references and appendices count when the paper prints them as headings.

dimensions.label: Missing headings
dimensions.question: Printed headings that the outline leaves out.

dimensions.label: Spurious headings
dimensions.question: Entries that are not printed headings (running heads, figure captions, invented titles).

dimensions.label: Wrong level or page
dimensions.question: Entries with the wrong nesting level or a page off by more than one.

components.label: Reading units
components.question: Does the logical segmentation group the paper into coherent units that a reader can take one at a time?
components.guidance: A good unit answers one question (what is the problem, how is it measured, what is the main result, does it survive robustness checks). It may merge several printed sections or split a long one.

dimensions.label: One idea per unit
dimensions.question: Does each unit answer one question, with boundaries where the argument turns?

anchors.0: Units are arbitrary page ranges, glue unrelated topics together, or mirror the outline with no grouping thought.
anchors.2: Most units hang together; one or two mix two questions or cut through an argument.
anchors.4: Every unit has a single job in the argument, and each boundary falls at a real turn.

dimensions.label: Granularity
dimensions.question: How many units, for this paper?

dimensions.label: Titles and summaries
dimensions.question: Does each title tell you what the unit gives you, and does each summary say faithfully and specifically what the unit establishes?

anchors.0: Genre labels (Introduction, Results), or summaries that could fit any paper or misstate a result.
anchors.2: A topic label on a result unit, or summaries that name the topic but not the finding or drop a material caveat.
anchors.4: Setup and method units name what they set up; result and interpretation units state the finding (for example 'The treatment is assigned by lottery, so the comparison is causal'); summaries are faithful and carry the load-bearing numbers.

components.label: Citation labels
components.question: For a sample of this paper's citation edges, does each label say correctly and specifically why the paper cites the work and what role the work plays in its argument?
components.guidance: The panel shows up to five labels sampled from the graph as it stands when the review opens (rejected labels left out), each with its relation, reason, quote, citing passage, the path that wrote it (paper reading or citation labeler) and its engagement, plus the last run's counts. Give each sampled label one verdict with a click; the summary counts the verdicts per label path and prompt version, so the grades are also labelled data for the next prompt. The accept, reject and edit actions you take in the literature graph are counted separately in the summary, so grading here does not replace reviewing there.

item_verdict.label: Verdict
item_verdict.question: The one main problem with this label, or ok.

options.label: Passage does not cite this work

dimensions.label: Navigable from above
dimensions.question: Read together, would these reasons let a newcomer see which works the paper stands on, tests or argues with, without opening the cited works?

anchors.2: Mostly right, but many reasons name a topic rather than what is taken, tested or disputed.
anchors.4: Each reason names the specific method, data, result or claim and what the paper does with it; passing mentions are honestly marked as such.

overall.label: Overall
overall.question: Would you trust the first view and the overview to orient a smart outsider to this paper?

anchors.0: Misleading; worse than reading the abstract alone.
anchors.2: Useful, but you would warn a friend about specific problems.
anchors.4: You would send it to a friend as the way into this paper.

issues.purpose: Flag each concrete problem you would want a prompt change to fix. Flags become regression cases, so quote the offending text when you can.

severities.label: Major: a reader would notice and lose trust
